facts.text: Woden’s name comes from the Norse god Odin, chosen after postal authorities rejected earlier names like Bingham and Ripley.
The Chicago, Rock Island and Pacific Railroad’s Klondike branch ran from Garner to Titonka, making Woden a grain shipping hub.
By 1907, Woden boasted a creamery, three general stores, a drug store, a meat market, a blacksmith, a livery stable, and a hotel.
The 2008 Midwest floods impacted north Iowa waterways, yet Woden experienced minimal inundation; historic droughts in the 1930s and 1950s stressed local aquifers.
